name: The Soulquarians (collective preset)
sources: style-research-extended-2 vol.2 neo-soul — The Soulquarians (collective preset)
Red Bull Music Academy — The Soulquarians (https://daily.redbullmusicacademy.com/2015/03/soulquarians-feature)
notes: The scene preset for the lane's core, based at Electric Lady with D'Angelo, Questlove, J Dilla and James Poyser at the centre; the entry says outright to "use as a global preset that other entries in this section inherit from". The band is the collective's stated 64–100 straight on 2&4 "with a heavy behind-the-beat drag", and the drum block is the working method: "1968 Ludwig kit, no click, first take, no overdubs; snare late, kick early, deliberate glitches inserted on purpose. Drum programming (Dilla's) and live drumming (Questlove's) are treated as the same instrument and are interchanged within a track." No click is `quantizeStrength` 0.42; the glitches are the wide snare window and the high `velocityVar`; the first-take-no-overdub rule is why the fills are pushed out to 8 and 16 bars. Harmony is described as "unconventional — offbeat rhythms, irregular chords", with m9/m11 tonics and "no functional cadence for bars at a time", so no progression families are authored at all and the delta is a triad weight of 0.03, a large `susSubstitutionProb` and long chord durations. The low end is "1950s-vintage bass guitars from the studio's collection plus Pino Palladino's Precision; no 808 or synth-sub anywhere in the collective's output" — hence no `bass808` block and a bass that climbs to 48 with the chord voicing lifted to 50 to clear it. The melody encodes the working method rather than a hook: jam-derived material, "songs settle into a mid-tempo groove with minimal verse-chorus-bridge progression", which is the long arc, the low chord-tone bias and the long intro/outro sections. ⚠ The INFERRED parameters are every drum probability and velocity band and all melody/countermelody numbers — the research documents membership, studio, gear and philosophy, not figures.
